words: مَنَعَ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُۥ وَسَعَىٰ فِى خَرَابِهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns those who block God's remembrance in mosques or work to ruin, disable, or repurpose them; such people have no relation to Paradise.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın mescidlerini içlerinde ism-i ilâhî zikredilmekten men‘eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulm is putting something outside its rightful place; the farther it is displaced, and the more sacred it is, the greater the injustice.
rows.anchor: Her şeyin hakkı, lâyık olduğu mevki‘e konulmak, zulüm de bir şeyi mevzi‘inin gayriye koymaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attacking mosques violates the rights of God, the mosques, and people, and opens perpetrators to every kind of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: hem Allah’ın, hem mescidlerin, hem de insanların

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is the greatest injustice; other verses use the same rhetorical question to say no greater rank of injustice exists.
rows.anchor: Nitekim وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mosques applies generally to every mosque, without exception.
rows.anchor: مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ terkîbi hiçbir istisnası olmayarak bütün mescidlere şâmildir ve âyetin hükmü umûmîdir.

rows.speaker: Cumhûr-i müfessirîn
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes identify the original occasion as the Temple's destruction and say the verse concerns Romans and Christians.
rows.anchor: Cumhûr-i müfessirînin beyânına göre asıl sebeb-i nüzul, Beyt-i Makdis’in tahrîbi meselesi olup âyet Rum ve Nasârâ hakkındadır.

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes instead say the verse concerns the polytheists.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirîn müşrikler hakkında olduğunu da beyan etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers that the verse encompass both Christians and polytheists because of their shared polytheistic traits and participation in mosque persecution; Roman Christians remain the principal target.
rows.anchor: En doğrusu her ikisi, yani Nasârâ’nın müşrikîn ile müşterek bulundukları hısâl-i şirk hakkındadır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Titus attacked Jerusalem, killed its people, enslaved their descendants, burned the Torah, destroyed the Temple, and left slaughtered pigs and carcasses inside.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden rivayet olunduğu vechile “Roma kayserlerinden Titos Kudüs’e hücum edip ahâlisini katl eylemiş, zürriyetlerini esir almış, Tevrat’ı yakmış, Beyt-i Makdis’i tahrip etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical accounts say Nebuchadnezzar first devastated the Temple and ended the Israelite state; Persian Ardashir Bahman later rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: Tarihlerin beyânına göre Beyt-i Makdis ilk defa Buhtunassar tarafından pek fecî bir surette tahrip edilmiş ve Benî İsrâil devletine nihâyet verilmiş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Persian reconstruction Israelites regrouped under Persian rule, then came under Greek and Roman rule; Zechariah and John were martyred in that period.
rows.anchor: Benî İsrâil yine toplanmış ve İran tâbiiyetinde bir hükûmet-i mahalliyeye nâil olmuştu, bilâhare Yunanlıların ve daha sonra Romalıların idaresine geçtiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: About forty years after Jesus' ascension, the Temple's second destruction began under Vespasian, Nero's successor, and was completed by Titus.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Îsâ’nın ‘urûcundan kırk sene kadar sonra da Kudüs’ün ve Beyt-i Makdis’in ikinci tahrîbi vâki‘oldu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus massacred Jerusalem's inhabitants, enslaved their children, plundered and destroyed the city and Temple, burned its books, and ended Israelite rule; Roman histories blame Israelite rebellion and excess.
rows.anchor: Titus da buraya şiddetle hücum ederek gizlenip kaçabilenlerden mâ‘adâ ahâlisini Yahudî olsun Hıristiyan olsun hep katliam ve zürriyetlerini tamamen esir etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Israel's punishment accords with the divine account that they disbelieved, killed prophets unjustly, disobeyed, and transgressed.
rows.anchor: beyân-ı ilâhîsi de bunu göstermiş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir says Emperor Hadrian, after sensing opposition, massacred many Jewish and Christian residents and destroyed the Temple for the last time.
rows.anchor: İbn Esîr’in Târîh-i Kâmil’de beyânına göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadrian rebuilt Jerusalem seven or eight years later, settled Romans and Greeks there, and erected a large statue to Venus; the city was renamed Ilya, reportedly meaning House of the Lord.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh yedi sekiz sene sonra şehri imar etmiş, Rum’dan, Yunan’dan birçok halk iskân eylemiş ve Zühre nâmına bir de büyük heykel bina etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Helena went to Jerusalem to find the cross Christians believed Jesus was crucified on and buried with; its discovery became the Christian Feast of the Cross.
rows.anchor: Roma’da Nasraniyet’i kabul ve ilan eden İstanbul bânîsi Kostantin’in anası Hilana (Eleni) Nasârâca Hazret-i Îsâ’nın üzerinde asıldığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Helena built the Holy Sepulchre over Jesus's supposed tomb, ordered the Temple remains cleared and rubbish dumped there, and Christians kept it a refuse heap and barred worship until Umar's time.
rows.anchor: o zamandan Hazret-i Ömer zamanına kadar Nasârâ orayı mezbele yapmışlar, orada Allah’a ibadet ve dua etmek isteyenleri men‘eylemişlerdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar found the site as a rubbish heap; Muslims then built al-Aqsa Mosque there.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer orayı mezbele halinde bulmuştu ve o zaman Mescid-i Aksâ Müslümanlar tarafından bina edilmiş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that Roman Christians joined and prolonged the Chaldean and Roman polytheists' persecution of the Temple, bearing greater responsibility; Jews also helped cause or failed to prevent its ruin.
rows.anchor: ve hatta daha devamlı bir surette iştirak etmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse summarizes these historical injustices, especially condemning Christians who shared in them, and generalizes reverence to all mosques.
rows.anchor: İşte bütün bu târihî mezâlimi icmal eden bu âyet-i kerîme bilhassa Nasârâ’nın müşriklere iştirak ettikleri bu zulme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its scope includes Jews, Christians, and polytheists, including Meccan polytheists barring the Prophet and Muslims from the Kaaba, and every past or future ban or destruction of a mosque.
rows.anchor: Ve binâen‘aleyh siyâk-ı âyet hem Yahudî ve hem Nasârâ’ya

words: مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلَّا خَآئِفِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressors have no right to enter those mosques except fearfully; if they enter, they should tremble for their lives, and God will eventually enforce this.
rows.anchor: Bunların o mescidlere korka korka girmeden başka hakk-ı duhulleri yoktur.

words: مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلَّا خَآئِفِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı sees the prophecy fulfilled when Jerusalem left Roman control, the Temple was rebuilt, and former oppressors could enter only fearfully; he draws a lesson for Muslims today.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Kur’ân’ın bu mucizesi zuhur etmiş, Kudüs Rumların elinden çıkmış, Beyt-i Makdis imar olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly disgrace means great calamity and deprivation: the perpetrators will lose state, strength, and power, and fall into subjection and ruin.
rows.anchor: o men‘ü zulmü yaptıran devletlerini, kuvvet ü şevketlerini zâyi‘edecek, mahkûmiyete düşecek, perişan olacaklardır.

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the worldly disgrace as the loss of Constantinople, the conquest of Istanbul.
rows.anchor: Şâyân-ı dikkattir ki Süddî tefsîrinde bu hızy u felâketten murad Kostantiniye şehrinin ellerinden çıkması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-Suddi's interpretation and its transmission in early authorities predate the conquest by centuries, Elmalılı treats it as a prophetic miracle transmitted by report.
rows.anchor: Bunlar İstanbul’un fethinden asırlarca mukaddem yazılmış olduğuna ve hele eslâf-ı müfessirînden olan Süddî beş altı asır mukaddem bulunduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In addition to worldly disgrace, these oppressors face immense afterlife punishment, which God will impose on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: bunlara dünyadaki o hızy u felâketten başka âhirette de pek büyük bir azab vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those barred from mosques and sincere worship should not despair or abandon God and worship; their opponents' claim to exclusive Paradise is unjust.
rows.anchor: me’yus olmamalı, ve o mescidlerden men‘edildik diye Allah’tan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the earth, with its east and west, belongs to God, not only the mosques from which worshippers may be excluded.
rows.anchor: sade o mescidler değil, bütün meşrık ve mağrib, yani bir tarafı meşrık ve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wherever people turn, they have a direction in which to worship God; God has no place and is beyond direction, though every direction belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: O’nun bir mekânı yoktur, Allah cihetten münezzehtir, fakat bütün cihetler de O’nundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer need not be performed in a mosque; people can pray toward any direction throughout pure earth, including in necessity.
rows.anchor: her cihete namaz kılınabilir ve Allah’ın rızâsına erilebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vāsiʿ means that God's mercy and power are expansive, He encompasses everything and accommodates His servants; He is not constrained and does not favor constriction.
rows.anchor: Vâsi‘dir, rahmet ü kudreti geniş, her şeyi muhît ve kullarına müsâadekârdır. Tahdid olunmaz, tazyîki sevmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse points to the juristic maxim that when a matter becomes constricted, it is expanded.
rows.anchor: Burada اَلأَْمْرُ إِذَا ضَاقَ اِتَّسَعَ kā‘ide-i fıkhiyesine işaret vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully knows worship wherever it occurs; the earlier qibla command was not due to hardship or ignorance, but to protect worshippers and train them in tawhid.
rows.anchor: Enbiyâya bir kıble emretmesi darlıktan veya ‘adem-i ilminden değil, kullarını vikāye ve sırr-ı tevhid ile terbiye etmek içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is vast and knowing, He can abrogate a previously commanded qibla and replace it with an equivalent or better one.
rows.anchor: Allah Vâsi‘ve ‘Alîm olduğu için mukaddemâ emrettiği bir kıbleyi nesh ederek ona mümasil ve hatta ondan daha hayırlı diğer bir kıbleye tahvil de edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse expansively permits prayer and serves as a fitting prelude and encouragement for the change of qibla.
rows.anchor: bu âyette namaz kılmak için büyük bir tevsi‘a ve tahvîl-i kıble emrine de güzel bir mukaddime ve güzel bir teşvik vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities could pray only in mosques, whereas Muslims were given the whole earth as a place of prayer.
rows.anchor: Ümem-i sâlife mescidlerden başka bir yerde namaz kılamazlarken Müslümanlara küre-i arzın her tarafı namazgâh yapılmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı presents the Kaaba, older than the Bayt al-Maqdis from which Jews were barred, as a qibla toward which they could be counseled in a way that appealed to their sentiments.
rows.anchor: Yahudîlere de memnû‘bulundukları Beytü’l-Makdis’den daha kadîm olan Kâbe’ye teveccüh için hissiyâtlarını okşayacak vechile güzel bir nasihat verilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı turns from the mosque oppressors to the Jews and Christians' further likeness to polytheists, introducing the following discussion.
rows.anchor: bunların müşriklere iştirâki sade bu kadar da değil daha var, dinleyiniz:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's nearness means that He promptly answers the person who calls on Him, not that He is near in place or direction.
rows.anchor: Demek ki Allah’ın yakınlığının mânası bu vehcile sür‘at-i icâbet demektir; kurb-i mekânî, kurb-i cihet demek değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebuts naturalists who imagine the Creator as a blind, deaf force and therefore deem prayer and worship useless.
rows.anchor: hâlık-ı kâinât olan Hak teâlâ’yı bilmez, işitmez, kör sağır bir kuvvet farz ederek namaz, oruç, dua gibi ibadetleri, müracaatları fâidesiz, lüzumsuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also rejects the Ijabiyya, who subject God's knowledge and will to fate and deny divine choice; denying God's creative power or knowledge is sheer ignorance.
rows.anchor: mebde’-i kader olan ilm-i ilâhîyi ve mebde’-i kazâ olan irâde-i ilâhiyeyi dahi bir kadere tâbi‘tutarak ihtiyâr-ı ilâhîyi inkâr eden Îcâbiyye’yi şiddetli bir red vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes people who shout and make a commotion in prayer because they imagine God is difficult to hear or far away.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı uzak zannedip de dualarında bağıranları red için nâzil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
rows.claim: In a battle, when the Companions raised their voices in takbir, tahlil, and prayer, the Prophet said they called neither a deaf nor an absent being, but One who hears and is near.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz “Siz, sağıra veya gāibe dua etmiyorsunuz, her hâlde bir semî‘-i karîbe dua ediyorsunuz” buyurmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One condition of prayer is humility and reverent concentration; God is nearer than the jugular vein and closer to people than they are to themselves.
rows.anchor: Bunun için duanın şerâitinden biri de hudû‘ve huşû‘dur. Zira insanlar Allah’tan uzak olsalar da “Allah karîb”dir, bize şah damarımızdan daha karîbdir

rows.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi argues that a possible thing receives existence only through its Maker, who stands between its essence and existence and is nearer to that essence than its existence is.
rows.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “İşbu فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ kavl-i ilâhîsinde bir sırr-ı aklî vardır. Şöyle ki, mâhiyyât-i mümkinâtın vücudlarıyla ittisâfı ancak îcâd-ı Sâni‘iledir.

rows.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi's higher argument says God causes not only possible essences to exist but each quiddity to be what it is, making Him nearer to every essence than it is to itself.
rows.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “İşbu فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ kavl-i ilâhîsinde bir sırr-ı aklî vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Razi's first argument treats essences as uncreated and the second as created; philosophers and Sufis accept the former, theologians the latter, with different conceptual priority between knowledge and will.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin birinci takrîri mâhiyyâtın gayr-i mec‘ûl olmasına, ikinci takrîri de mec‘ûl olmasına göredir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the source of every necessity: possible existence derives from Necessary Existence, as do universal matters and possible essences; without God there is neither existence nor logic.
rows.anchor: Vücûdât-ı mümkine vücûd-ı vâcibden müstefâd olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating possible essences as eternally uncreated would multiply self-necessary principles or posit a principle binding God, contradicting God's sole status as First Cause.
rows.anchor: Böyle bir iddia bizâtihi ve lizâtihi mebâdî-i zarûriyenin, lizâtihi vâcibü’l-vücûdun ta‘addüdüne kāil olmaktır. Hâlbuki bizâtihi ve lizâtihi illetü’l-‘ilel birdir, o da Allah teâlâ’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the necessary judgment that a thing is itself ultimately depends on considering God's necessary existence; all truth-assent depends on affirming the Necessary Being.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle her nefsü’l-emr tasdîki, tasdîk-i vâcibe mütevakkıftır. Binâen‘aleyh bütün vücûbların, zarûretlerin menşe’i Cenâb-ı Hak’tır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people hear and answer one another's hopes and requests, they must believe that God, nearer to them than they are to themselves, hears their prayers even sooner.
rows.anchor: biz kendimizin ve başkalarının recâ ve temenniyâtını duyup bilebiliyor ve onlara işittiğimiz zaman cevap da verebiliyorsak, bize bizden daha yakın olan Allah teâlâ’nın dualarımızı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duʿāʾ is originally a verbal noun meaning calling, like daʿwat; conventionally it means a subordinate's request or entreaty to a superior and is also used as a noun.
rows.anchor: “Duâ”, esasen “da‘vet” gibi çağırmak mânasına masdardır. Sonra küçükten büyüğe, aşağıdan yukarıya vâki‘olan taleb ü niyaz mânasına örf olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reality of prayer is the servant's seeking help, care, and assistance from the Lord.
rows.anchor: Duanın hakikati, kulun Rabbi celle celâluhu’dan istimdad ve inâyet ü me‘ûnet istid‘â etmesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects as ignorant the claim that prayer is useless, especially among advocates of a blind natural force and adherents of necessitarian or compulsion theories.
rows.anchor: İlimden dem vuran bazı câhiller duâyı fâidesiz bir şey zannetmişlerdir. Bunların başında kudret-i fâtırayı bir kuvvet-i ‘amyâ zu‘m eden kör kuvvetçiler vardır.

rows.speaker: Îcâb veya cebir nazariyelerine saplananlar
rows.claim: The objectors argue that a request already known by God to occur must occur necessarily, while one not known to occur is impossible, so prayer is needless either way.
rows.anchor: Bunlardan başka îcab veya cebir nazariyelerine saplananlardan da bu babda birtakım şüpheler îrâdına kalkışanlar olmuştur. Şöyle ki: 1. Dua ile matlub

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second fatalist objection says events are fixed by an eternal cause: what it decreed is necessary, what it did not decree impossible, so prayer can neither increase nor decrease destiny.
rows.anchor: Bu âlemdeki bütün hâdisâtın bir müessir-i kadîme müntehî olduğunda şüphe yoktur. O hâlde bu müessir-i kadîmin ezelde vücûdunu iktizâ ettiği şey

rows.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying God determined destinies a certain number of years before creating creation; Elmalılı gives no grading.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz bile “قَدَّرَ اللّٰهُّٰ الْمَقَادِيرَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ الْخَلْقَ بِكَذَا وَكَذَا عَامًا: Allah mekādîri, halkı halk etmezden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı also cites the saying that the pen has dried concerning what will be.
rows.anchor: kezâlik جَفَّ الْقَلَمُ بِمَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ buyurmamış mıdır?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a hadith that four matters are already finished: lifespan, provision, creation, and character; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: Dört şeyden ferâgat hâsıl olmuştur: Ömür, rızık, halk, ahlâk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as God answers their prayers, people must answer His call and believe in Him.
rows.anchor: O hâlde onlar da Benim davetime koşsunlar ve Bana hakkıyla iman etsinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding to God and believing in Him enables people to proceed in right guidance.
rows.anchor: ki rüşd ile gidebilsinler
